evals.prompt: Do a style review of this excerpt of a deephaven-core concept guide: .claude/skills/deephaven-writing-style/evals/files/awk-excerpt.md. Report only — don't edit anything.
evals.expected_output: Flags the real paragraphs Chip Kent called awkward (GIL paragraph, barrier definition, execution-order sentence, implicit-barriers opener, configuration intro) as needing unusual punctuation to be grammatical, reports it as one pattern, proposes rewrites in plain short sentences or a bullet list, and leaves the two clean paragraphs alone.
expectations: Flags the GIL paragraph ('Most Python builds use the GIL ...' with its semicolon) as hard to read because of its punctuation or compound structure, and proposes splitting it into separate sentences
Flags the Barrier definition paragraph (colon, bold terms, and a semicolon in one sentence) as hard to read and proposes plain separate sentences or a short list
Flags the 'Execution order: A and B run in parallel ...' paragraph and proposes a bullet list with one bullet per column (or equivalent enumeration)

Flags the implicit-barriers opener ('When implicit barriers are enabled ... — two serial columns ... without explicit barriers:' ) as needing a dash and colon to be grammatical and proposes splitting it
Flags the configuration intro ('Parallelization needs no configuration. These properties tune it; defaults ...') as relying on a semicolon and proposes plain sentences

Reports the problem as one named pattern (a paragraph that needs unusual punctuation such as colons, em dashes, parentheticals, or semicolons to be grammatical) rather than only as unrelated one-off comments
Rewritten text offered for the flagged paragraphs contains no semicolons and no em-dash or parenthetical asides inside a sentence
Control: does not flag the 'Updates' paragraph under Query phases, or the 'Column A gets values 0–9. Column B gets values 10–19.' paragraph, as hard to read

No proposed rewrite or replacement text puts a configuration property name or default into narrative prose (a separate sentence in the same paragraph counts); precise values are sent to a Configuration section or a reference link

Control: does not flag as hard to read the 'The three mechanisms above apply to operations that compute and store their results when they run:' sentence (a colon introducing a bullet list), the 'To fix this, create a `Selectable` object and apply `with_serial`:' sentence (a colon introducing a code block), or the 'Most users don't need to change this setting — see Configuration.' sentence (one dash before a pointer)
